newsitem.title: USA: Cold, rains slow Texas Plains cotton maturity.
newsitem.headline: Cold, rains slow Texas Plains cotton maturity.

text.p: Unseasonably cold, rainy weather slowed cotton maturity in the Texas Plains during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
"Although the much-needed rains have revived pastures with lush growth and provided moisture for small grain planting, rains continued to cause problems for cotton harvesting," the report said.
Cotton quality continued to decline as as growers could not get it out of the fields in central Texas.
Wheat planted 65 percent vs 41 year ago, 45 average.
Wheat emerged 40 percent vs 19 y/a, 23 avg.
Corn harvested 74 percent vs 80 y/a, 78 avg.
Corn mature 96 percent vs 94 y/a, 92 avg.
Sorghum harvested 62 percent vs 75 y/a, 73 avg.
Sorghum mature 84 percent vs 88 y/a, 83 avg.
Sorghum rated 55 pct good/excellent, 36 fair, 9 poor/v.poor.
Cotton bolls opening 57 percent vs 55 y/a, 52 avg.
Cotton harvested 18 percent vs 25 y/a, 25 avg.
Cotton rated 51 pct good/excellent, 23 fair, 26 poor/v.poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 45 pct good to excellent, versus 41 percent at that level last week.
